=== COLUMN 1 ===
BAY
One of the most
consistent drivers
on the USAC stock
car circuit has to be
Wilbur "Bay" Dar-
nell of Deerfield,
Ill., who is now in
his ninth year of
competition in the
stocks.
Russ Lake Photo
A veteran of short track racing in northern Illinois and southern Wisconsin, Darnell was a frequent competitor
on the old quarter-mile Fair Park dirt oval, having credit for one modified feature win on that track.
In 1962 he drove his first USAC stock car race in a 1961 Ford. He gained little more than experience that
first year, finishing 21st in the point standings. He displayed steady improvement, however, and by 1966, he fin-
ished sixth in the standings with an equally high showing in 1967.
Darnell drove his first USAC Championship car event in 1965, placing ninth at DuQuoin, Ill. He continued
driving the smaller cars until early in the 1968 season when he was badly burned in an accident at Milwaukee in
June which took the life of Ronnie Duman.
Though it took a while for him to regain his old form, he was back in action by the end of 1968.

A veteran of short track racing in northern Illinois and southern Wisconsin, Darnell was a frequent competitor
on the old quarter-mile Fair Park dirt oval, having credit for one modified feature win on that track.
In 1962 he drove his first USAC stock car race in a 1961 Ford. He gained little more than experience that
first year, finishing 21st in the point standings. He displayed steady improvement, however, and by 1966, he fin-
ished sixth in the standings with an equally high showing in 1967.
Darnell drove his first USAC Championship car event in 1965, placing ninth at DuQuoin, Ill. He continued
driving the smaller cars until early in the 1968 season when he was badly burned in an accident at Milwaukee in
June which took the life of Ronnie Duman.
Though it took a while for him to regain his old form, he was back in action by the end of 1968.
He ranks 13th in the all-time USAC stock car point standings and, although he has often been a front-runner, he
is still looking for his first USAC late model victory.
